newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan, US to hold preparatory air talks in January.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US to hold preparatory air talks in January.

text.p: Japan and the United States will hold a preparatory meeting in January to discuss various aviation issues to pave the way for a resumption of negotiations which have been deadlocked since August, the Transport Ministry said on Tuesday.
Transport Minister Makoto Koga told a news conference that senior officials of both countries would hold an unofficial meeting In Tokyo on January 10 to discuss aviation issues.
Their bilateral dispute centres on the granting of "beyond" rights to U.S. carriers to operate flights from the United States to Japan and onward to other Asian countries.
Washington has argued that a 1952 bilateral aviation agreement allows for beyond rights for U.S. carriers but Japan says such rights have been granted only in exceptional cases.
Japan has refused to approve new flights unless the United States grants extra flights to Japanese carriers.
A senior U.S. Transportation Department official said last week that the United States would put emphasis on reaching "open skies" accords in Asian markets next year.
Mark Gerchick, deputy assistant secretary for aviation and international affairs, said that Japan was the key in Asia's fast-growing aviation market.
